THE STORY BEHIND HER

A life made of little moments.

Some lives are made of big moments. Others are made of little ones — school days, inside jokes, awkward beginnings, friendships, questions, changes, and the quiet moments when you realise you are becoming someone new.

This is Meelah's story so far: a collection of chapters about where she came from, the people and places that shaped her, and the person she is still becoming.

“Your memories deserve more than a camera roll. They deserve a story.”
A LITTLE NOTE, JUST FOR YOU

For every version of you.

There are so many things about you that could never fit into a few pages — the little things you do without thinking, the moments you probably do not realise anyone remembers, the laughs, the difficult days, the people you have loved, and all the versions of yourself you have grown through.

This story is not meant to capture every single moment. It is simply a place to keep some of them safe — the pieces of your life that deserve to be remembered exactly because they were yours.

So whenever you come back to these pages, I hope you remember not only what happened, but who you were when it happened.

And when you look back at the person on these pages, I hope you are gentle with her. She was learning. She was trying. She was growing. She did not have to have everything figured out yet.

You were becoming. And you still are.

CHAPTER 01LOREVA

Once Upon a Beginning

Once upon a beginning, there was a little girl named Moyinoluwa.

She was short, charming, and felt things deeply. She was also always eating, somehow finding her way to food like it was part of her daily responsibilities.

She could be goofy. She could be soft-hearted. And whenever there was tension around her, she somehow found herself trying to make peace.

She was still figuring herself out, but even then, there was something about her that made her, well… her.

↑ BACK TO CHAPTERS
CHAPTER 02LOREVA

Finding Her Way

She grew up in Lagos, Nigeria, where one chapter naturally led into another.

She went to Goldscholars Model School and eventually graduated. She spent some time in Tahfiz, then later moved on to Ansarud Deen College, Isolo.

At first, stepping into a new school felt like stepping into a room where everyone already knew where they belonged. She entered like a novice and had to find her rhythm. Eventually, she blended in.

School became more than just classes and exams. It became one of the places where she changed, learned, met people, and slowly discovered different versions of herself.

↑ BACK TO CHAPTERS
CHAPTER 03LOREVA

School, Life & Everything In Between

Somewhere along the way, she started a business because, honestly, she liked money. Fair enough.

School had its own twists and turns too. She stopped for a while, then returned. There were the looks, the comments, the moments when people had something to say.

But somehow, buh, she scaled through.

By final year, she was still very much an average student — not the brilliant one everyone expected to become a professor, and definitely not failing either. She was simply doing her thing.

She was not exactly every teacher's favourite, but at least she finished. And along the way, she met many people. Some became part of her life. Some became history.

↑ BACK TO CHAPTERS
CHAPTER 04LOREVA

And Then There Was Meelah

By the time final year came around, she already knew a lot of people.

So this chapter was not really about creating an entirely new circle. It was about stronger bonds with people who were already around her — conversations that became deeper, friendships that became more familiar, and moments that slowly mattered more.

And somewhere in the middle of all of that, Meelah appeared.

Not suddenly. Not dramatically. Just gradually — through the people she met, the things she experienced, and the person she was becoming.

↑ BACK TO CHAPTERS
CHAPTER 05LOREVA

Meet Meelah

Final year was not easy.

There were exams, pressure, emotions, friendships, and the general chaos that comes with trying to finish school while also trying to understand yourself.

Still, she kept showing up.

She laughed. She went out. She smiled. She could have a lot on her mind and still look completely fine.

Meelah took shape through that quiet strength. She was funny and playful. She liked going out. She was learning how to balance exams, friendships, feelings, and life — sometimes perfectly, sometimes not so perfectly.

Moyinoluwa slowly became Meelah. Not because the old her disappeared, but because she grew into someone new.

↑ BACK TO CHAPTERS
CHAPTER 06LOREVA

Meelah Being Meelah

Then came the part where Meelah started talking a lot.

And of course, people had opinions. Some called her annoying.

Did she care? Not particularly.

She had goals. She loved reading novels, and books became one of the things that kept her going, along with the people she cared about most.

Final year brought its own personal issues too. She fell out with some people, became closer to others, worked on herself, and found people who became important to her.

Through all of it, she was still becoming herself.

↑ BACK TO CHAPTERS
CHAPTER 07LOREVA

So… What Now?

Then, just like that, school was finished.

Her grades were average — not brilliant, not terrible. Just hers.

For a while, she considered modeling. She loved modeling, loved good photos, and knew she could look good in front of a camera. She gave it a try, but it did not work out the way she imagined.

And maybe that was okay.

Trying things is part of figuring yourself out. After school, there was no timetable telling her what came next. No obvious next answer.

Just one question sitting quietly in front of her:

“What next?”

↑ BACK TO CHAPTERS
CHAPTER 08LOREVA

Her Own Space

After school, she fell out with most of her friends because of different personal moments.

But she was not afraid to restart.

She could let things go. She could step back. Sometimes, she simply wanted her own space — her books, her thoughts, and her favourite people when she felt like being around them.

She started ghosting the world a little.

Not because she had stopped caring, but because she was learning that she did not always need a crowd around her.

Sometimes starting over means removing the noise long enough to hear yourself again.

And Meelah was still finding her way.

She would figure it out in her own time, in her own way, in her own Meelah way.
